group.passage:
English gets by with just 26 letters, yet Japanese students must learn about two thousand symbols before they have the basic tools for reading and writing. Why do the world's writing systems differ so greatly in size? The main reason lies in how large a piece of language each symbol stands for, as the table below shows.
The smallest piece is a single sound: in an alphabet, one letter usually represents one consonant or one vowel, so a few dozen letters are enough. Korean Hangeul is a famous example. Writing Korean with Chinese characters was once so hard that most people could not read, so in 1443 King Sejong created a new alphabet of 28 letters that ordinary people could learn easily. Four of those letters later fell out of use, and unlike English, Korean groups its letters into blocks, one block for each syllable. Arabic works differently again, since its letters mostly stand for consonants, while short vowels are shown by small marks that are rarely used in everyday writing.
Devanagari, the script used for Hindi, takes a middle path. Every consonant letter already includes a short "a" sound, so the letter for k is read as "ka." To produce a different vowel, a writer attaches a small mark to the consonant instead of writing a separate letter. Japanese kana go one step further, since each basic symbol stands for a whole syllable, such as "ka" or "mi."
At the far end are Chinese characters, which carry meaning as well as sound. Because each character has a meaning of its own, thousands of them are needed. Taiwan's Ministry of Education lists 4,808 common characters, 6,334 less common ones and 18,388 rare ones, while Japan, which mixes characters with kana, has an official list of 2,136 for everyday use.
A large set of symbols is not simply better or worse than a small one. Learners can get used to a new set of a few dozen letters in a week or two, but each letter on its own tells the reader only a sound. A character takes far longer to learn, yet it packs both sound and meaning into a single sign. Every writing system, in its own way, strikes a balance between these two needs.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.B: How King Sejong created an alphabet for ordinary Koreans.
options.C: Why alphabets are easier to read than other kinds of writing.

questions.stem: Based on the passage and the table, which of the following is true?

options.A: Hangeul has more letters today than when King Sejong created it.
options.B: The Arabic script has the fewest basic symbols of any system in the table.
options.C: Japanese hiragana has more basic symbols than Devanagari does.

questions.stem: Based on the passage, how would a writer using Devanagari most likely write the syllable “ki”?

options.A: By writing the k letter followed by a separate i letter.
options.B: By marking the k letter with a vowel sign.
options.C: By using one symbol that stands for the whole syllable “ki.”
options.D: By writing only the k letter and letting the reader supply the vowel.

questions.stem: Which best describes the author's view of writing systems that use thousands of symbols?

options.A: Critical, since they keep many people from learning to read.
options.B: Admiring, since they are plainly superior to alphabets.
options.C: Doubtful, since their official lists keep changing.
options.D: Balanced, since they bring a benefit as well as a cost.

translation_zh.text:
英文只用 26 個字母就夠了，日本學生卻必須學會大約兩千個符號，才算具備讀寫的基本工具。為什麼世界上各種文字系統的規模差這麼多？主要原因在於每個符號代表的語言單位有多大，如下表所示。
最小的單位是單一的音：在字母系統裡，一個字母通常代表一個子音或一個母音，所以幾十個字母就夠用了。韓文是一個著名的例子。過去用漢字書寫韓語非常困難，大多數人都不識字，所以世宗大王在 1443 年創造了一套有 28 個字母、一般百姓也能輕鬆學會的新字母。其中四個字母後來不再使用；而且和英文不同，韓文把字母組成一個個方塊，每個方塊是一個音節。阿拉伯文又是另一種做法：它的字母大多代表子音，短母音則用小記號表示，而日常書寫很少標出這些記號。
用來書寫印地語的天城文走的是中間路線。每個子音字母本身就帶有一個短的「a」音，所以 k 這個字母讀作「ka」。要變成其他母音時，書寫者是在子音上加一個小記號，而不是另外寫一個字母。日文的假名更進一步，每個基本符號代表一整個音節，例如「ka」或「mi」。
另一端則是漢字，漢字同時承載意義和聲音。由於每個字都有自己的意思，所需的字就以千計。台灣教育部列出 4,808 個常用字、6,334 個次常用字和 18,388 個罕用字；混用漢字與假名的日本，則有一份收錄 2,136 字的日常使用字表。
符號多並不單純比符號少更好或更差。學習者一兩週就能熟悉一套幾十個字母，但每個字母本身只告訴讀者一個音。一個漢字要花更長的時間學，卻能把聲音和意義都裝進一個符號裡。每一種文字系統都以自己的方式，在這兩種需求之間取得平衡。
【表】六種文字系統：拉丁字母（字母；一個符號通常代表一個子音或母音；26 個；英文）、韓文（字母；代表子音或母音，組成音節方塊；24 個；韓語）、阿拉伯字母（輔音音素文字；大多代表子音；28 個；阿拉伯語）、天城文（元音附標文字；帶有內建「a」音的子音，或一個母音；44 個；印地語）、平假名（音節文字；一個音節；46 個；日語）、漢字（語素文字；一個意義單位及其讀音；台灣常用字表 4,808 字；中文）。

open_tasks.prompt: Choose two writing systems from the table. In 1–2 English sentences, explain why one of them needs many more symbols than the other.
reference_answers: Hiragana needs more symbols than the Latin alphabet because each hiragana symbol stands for a whole syllable, while each Latin letter stands for only one sound.
Chinese characters need thousands of symbols, while Hangeul needs only 24, because each character carries its own meaning but each Hangeul letter stands for just a consonant or a vowel.

有沒有用「一個符號代表什麼」來解釋差異
